svg.text: B1 · PR #480 as written — node-b answers in 1.2 s (20 % over the interval)
Skip rule: after a poll, if next_cycle ≤ now → forfeit int(overrun/interval)+1 slots. A slot fires only exactly
largest node-b row gap = 2.0 s (row timestamps = request midpoints)
node-b keeps 3 of node-a's 7 slots (50 %). Largest node-b row gap 2.0 s.
missed_sample_ranges: node-b seq 1 (sample_schedule_overrun), node-b seq 3 (sample_schedule_overrun), node-b seq
Skip rule: forfeit only if next_cycle + interval ≤ now → int(overrun/interval) slots. Slot N may start any time
largest node-b row gap = 1.2 s (row timestamps = request midpoints)
node-b keeps 5 of 7 slots (physical ceiling 1/1.2 = 83 %). Largest row gap 1.2 s = the request latency.
seq is still the slot index (start + seq·interval); node-b's row for seq N is simply taken later inside slot N —
bounded by < 1 interval, re-synced on every skip (sawtooth, no drift).
C1 · PR #480 as written — node-b's seq 1 hangs 4 s (2 × timeout); stop fires at 4.5 s mid-flight
Stop sets _stop; each thread leaves its loop and does one bracket poll at whatever seq it holds. The in-loop
largest node-b row gap = 5.0 s (row timestamps = request midpoints)
node-a was idle waiting for slot 5 → brackets at seq 5 (t ≈ 4.6). node-b's hung request settles after stop →
skip block suppressed → brackets at seq 2 at t ≈ 5.1: 3 slots behind, same wall-clock.
Slots 2–4 on node-b are never recorded: missed_sample_ranges = node-b seq 1 (endpoint_timeout). The undercount
is silent — the validator only checks per-host consistency.
C2 · Prototype — same hang, bracket seq derived from the clock: B = floor(t_stop / interval) + 1 = 5
Computed once in stop_and_finalize. Each thread: if B > its counter → record counter…B−1 as
sample_schedule_overrun; then poll seq B with scheduled_at = grid time of B.
largest node-b row gap = 5.0 s (row timestamps = request midpoints)
Both hosts bracket at seq 5. node-b fills the gap as one coalesced range: node-b seq 1 (endpoint_timeout),
Every thread's counter is ≤ S+1 at stop (it cannot have polled a slot that has not started) and an idle thread
holds exactly S+1 — so B never collides with an existing row and never goes backwards.
Bracket row timestamps: node-a ≈ 4.6 (fires at stop), node-b ≈ 5.1 (fires when its hung request settles). Same
seq, skew bounded by one request latency; the validator only needs a row with t ≥ window end.
